suggestions.assertion: The design tokens locked decision from v2.0 is preserved / The src/legacy/ freeze decision from v2.0 is preserved / The constraint that only Priya has staging/production database access is preserved
suggestions.reason: These three pass on the presence of a recognisable string. A rewrite that demoted the freeze to a suggestion, dropped 'Status: Final', or lost the rationale/date/approval-source would still pass. Consider tightening to require the decision retain its Final status plus at least its date and approval source - that is what actually makes a locked decision survive a cumulative merge.

suggestions.assertion: Updated Master is at most 14,000 characters
suggestions.reason: This is the most discriminating assertion in the set and it correctly caught the one real regression (16,172 chars). Worth keeping, but consider pairing it with a lower soft target reported as a metric (e.g. chars-per-section, or ratio to the previous version) so iteration-3 can see whether it is trending toward the cap or away from it - a binary pass/fail hides a 25,349 -> 16,172 improvement entirely.

No assertion checks that the source Daily handoffs are left unmodified. A skill that 'incorporates' Dailies by rewriting or deleting them would pass all 18 assertions. The run did the right thing here (both Dailies byte-identical to the fixtures) but nothing tests for it.

No assertion rewards or checks the accuracy of newly-added repo-derived facts. The output makes many precise, checkable claims (commit a3549a9, jose 5.9.6, TTL at session.ts line 6, the 'dev-only-secret' fallback) and every one is correct - genuinely the strongest evidence that the skill verified rather than confabulated. An assertion like 'technical state matches the actual repo (commit hash, branch, dependency versions) and any new risk cited points to a real line of code' would discriminate hard against a run that just paraphrased the Dailies.

Assertion 17 ('every inherited claim that could not be verified is labelled') is nearly impossible to grade exhaustively and forces the grader to draw the line between repo-checkable and organisational claims. Consider naming the specific traps - the 7c21ab4 commit, 'build/test passing', the missing 2026-07-24 Daily, and the three absent paths - so the verdict is mechanical.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1-14 are largely mechanical string/structure checks that a careful run passes easily; 15-18 carry the real discriminating power, and 15 is the only one that failed. The set has a blind spot around source-file integrity and around the accuracy (as opposed to the presence) of newly-added facts.
